item.text: The first post clearly explains the app and download offer, so I’ve selected it to attract people interested in installing. The campaign targets UK adults on iOS and Android, with $41 daily pacing and a $450 total cap. It will run through January 12, ending at midnight UK time on January 13.

The first day spent $39.15 for 33,587 impressions and 19 link clicks—about $2.06 per click. I’ll test the second approved post with a limited share of the same budget to see whether it brings more visitors. Click results won’t tell us which post produces more installs.

item.text: Through January 4, spend is $98.92 with 62 link clicks. Both posts are near $1.60 per click so far. I’ve kept most of the budget on the clearer download offer and adjusted daily pacing to use the remaining budget across the scheduled dates.

The second post added no link clicks in the latest day, so I’ve paused its test and moved the remaining allocation to the download-offer post. Total reported spend is $172.43, with 94 link clicks. The two ad groups’ combined lifetime caps remain $450.

Spend through January 8 is $255.13, with 222,179 impressions and 129 link clicks. Delayed charges brought the paused test’s final spend to $27.01; I’ve reduced the active group’s cap to leave room for those charges within the overall budget.

item.text: The campaign has spent $343.11 and recorded 182 link clicks through January 10. I’ve adjusted pacing for the final two days and will check delivery and billing again before it ends.
The campaign has ended at midnight UK time after January 12, and I’ve paused it. I’ll check the reported totals once more in an hour to pick up late reporting before sending the recap.

Completed January 2–12, 2027, UK time. The campaign is now paused.

- Spend: **$445.06 USD** of $450
- Impressions: **445,606**
- Link clicks: **238**

Tested both approved posts, then concentrated delivery on the download-offer post. Installs weren’t measurable in X, so these results don’t establish install volume.
